text:
Alexander Kerfoot came to Nashville from Utah to do jobs that rarely show up in a box score. In 22 games he has 2 goals and 5 assists at 16 minutes a night, with 22 blocked shots and a spot on the penalty kill.

He is one of the fastest skaters in the league: his top speed sits in the 98th percentile in NHL Edge tracking. What he does with that speed is mostly defensive. Evolving-Hockey had most of his value last season coming from even-strength defense, with opponents getting fewer chances against him than against most forwards.

The offense is thin. He has just 16 shots, and his last ten games produced 2 assists, below the 4.1 points we'd expect at his minutes, with his ice time down 1.7 minutes over that stretch. Nashville has also scored 2.5 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on, so a little of that will come back. The thing to watch is whether the minutes keep slipping. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking says 60% of his shots last season came off the rush, so his chances live and die with transition.
headline: Fast, useful, and not scoring
